name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd
title: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd - 543412 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Fifth straight quarter of underwriting improvement: Q2 underwriting profit Rs 99 crore vs loss of Rs 40 crore, CISR 98% (improved 2.9 pts), but no numeric FY27 guidance was repeated and reported growth is inflated by 1/n multi-year accounting.

summary.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. Normalized PAT (at an 8% investment yield) rose 70% YoY to Rs 390 crore in Q2. Management flagged that headline growth will moderate in H2 as last year's GST-led surge enters the base, and that regulatory proposals on distribution commissions and expense of management (EoM) are the next key uncertainty.

segments.name: Retail health (fresh)
segments.commentary: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% YoY in Q2 and 36% in H1 on reported 1/n basis; new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% from 89%, with new-to-insurance policies up over 10% and average sum insured up 13%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Network reached 8.7 lakh agents after adding 39,000 in H1; agency productivity up 19% YoY; agency contributes about 70-75% of fresh business and grew about 25% in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C grew 137% YoY in H1 and its share of business rose from 8% to 13%; management says D2C has superior combined ratios. Proprietary channels (agency plus D2C) account for over 90% of retail business.

segments.name: Renewal book
segments.commentary: Management says the standalone renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio; vintage book is about 80% of portfolio. Group business is now a very small share of premium.

guidance_outlook: Company aspires to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently over a long period and hopes to maintain that for FY27, though optical growth moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4 due to GST-led base.
ROE ambition to move from mid-teens to higher-teens over time, with combined ratio as the key lever.
Retail market share and like-for-like comparability under 1/n reporting expected to be restored only by FY28.
Management believes it has a credible path to the proposed EoM limits through operating leverage, productivity and digitization, but will give more detail once regulation is final.
Company will not disclose point-to-point guidance on individual loss ratio metrics.
capex_capacity: Equity allocation about 14% (slightly less than 14%), with internal strategy to cap at around 15%; management may go beyond 15% if markets are very attractive.

Portfolio duration increased toward a target of about 4 years after G-Sec yields rose; management said it has taken some long-duration G-Sec calls and may extend duration further if yields keep rising.
REITs and InvITs: fully invested against the 3% regulatory limit with a small margin of safety; AIF allocation about 2.1-2.2% of funds and growing slowly.
Digital SBU created last year; Salesforce CRM upgraded; AI bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume at under 20% of human cost.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is driven by a mix of price, volume and higher average sum insured; management did not split the contribution.
Around 80% of the book was repriced in the last cycle; the remaining portion is being repriced this year, with further correction as needed based on loss ratios.
Packages account for about 80% of claims; hospital negotiations described as business as usual, with the Supreme Court drug-pricing order not yet notified.
Management estimates a fresh-to-insurance market share near 40% (not a reported figure) and notes the reported fresh figure includes portability.
Commission ratio moderated YoY because the senior citizen commission cut (15% to 10%) and other efficiencies now show a full 12-month impact.

qa_highlights.question: How is fresh growth tracking in October and by channel, now that the GST-led base is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects optical moderation in Q3 and Q4 but aims for 20%+ fresh growth; it tracks policies sold, agent activations and digital activations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the loss ratio improvement driven by fresh business or by the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Improvement is driven by the vintage book (about 80% of portfolio), since the fresh book at about 20% of the portfolio could not drive it alone; renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio. Fresh and renewal loss ratios are not disclosed separately.

qa_highlights.question: Loss ratio decomposition in Q2 (frequency, severity, pricing) and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss cost held at mid-single-digit growth while earned premium grew close to double digits; management did not give point-to-point metric guidance and will focus on combined ratio going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Equity and duration positioning, and whether there is an equity cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity about 14%, no incremental purchases this quarter; the 15% level is an internal strategy, not a formal cap. Duration lengthened toward about 4 years via G-Sec calls.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to the Rs 59 crore investment-related loss and its FVTPL classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity, ETFs, REITs and InvITs are classified as FVTPL; debt is held to maturity. No breakdown of the Rs 59 crore between realized and unrealized was provided in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the insurance finance income and expense restatement, and will it stay nil?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance finance income and expense (significant financing component on long-term policies) was discontinued as an optional treatment; it is now nil and has no PAT impact because the offsetting income sits in restated insurance revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How are multi-year policies commissioned, and what is the impact of the proposed distribution rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Multi-year policies are around 50% of the fresh book; good agents are paid upfront under Indian GAAP and the amount is deferred under IFRS; clarification is awaited on whether years two and three count as fresh or renewal under the new rules.

risks_watch: Optical moderation of fresh growth in Q3 and Q4 as the GST-driven base builds.

IRDAI distribution reform (commission linked to renewal rates, agent exclusivity, higher rural commissions) and whether the EoM cap of 20% can be met without major OpEx changes; the calculation was not disclosed.
Treatment of multi-year policy commissions (years two and three) under the new distribution rules; about 50% of fresh book is multi-year.
Dark-pattern and data consent norms for D2C, which is growing rapidly.
Supreme Court drug-pricing order and its effect on itemized hospital bills (about 20% of claims are non-package).
Investment book sensitivity to rising yields and a planned RBI policy rate hike cycle.
summary.management_tone: Confident on underwriting turnaround and structural sustainability, but guarded on specifics: management declined to split growth drivers, disclose the loss ratio by fresh and renewal, quantify telemedicine savings, or give the Rs 59 crore investment-loss breakdown. On regulation it is supportive of the direction but explicitly awaiting final rules.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 of FY27 has marked the 5th successive quarter of improvement in our loss ratios and underwriting results.
The fresh book at around 20% slice of the portfolio could not have driven outcomes on its own.
As a company, we aspire to grow at 20% plus on fresh business consistently for a long period of time.

growth.why: Management aspires to 20%+ fresh business growth consistently and expects to hold it for FY27, though optical moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4; Q2 GWP grew 19% YoY on a reported 1/n basis, backed by agency expansion (8.7 lakh agents, productivity up 19%), D2C growth of 137% and repricing, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given.
